source: the regex-timeout replay reads the pattern as Pattern.compile does, so a catastrophic pattern written in Java-only syntax (class intersection, \h, \p{javaLetter}, \p{InBasic_Latin}, \Q…\E, a named group) passes regexMatchingTimeoutMillis (here 300) on a 40-character value and logs the WARN `regex evaluation timed out after {}ms for pattern:{}— treating as non-match`, in RegexStringMatcher (DOTALL | CASE_INSENSITIVE | UNICODE_CASE: an upper-case pattern letter folds) and in GraphQL's operationName (Pattern.compile(p)); a short value fails within the budget

steps.note: class intersection: Java backtracking passes the budget
class intersection on a short path: no timeout
